title: fix(gateway): keep tunnel requests on their intended route
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Some OpenClaw ID tunnel requests with unusual body headers or WebSocket paths can reach an unintended Gateway route.

## User Impact

Tunneled HTTP requests retain their streamed bodies and requested routes across shared ingress connections. WebSocket upgrades use the configured local ingress socket. No configuration or migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The tunnel child now rebuilds HTTP request framing from the bytes it sends and pins WebSocket connections to its configured Unix socket. The workspace upload reader accepts framed requests without a declared length while retaining its streaming byte limit. Response body headers remain intact.

## Evidence

- A sandboxed, two-revision run drove synthetic streams through the production HTTP and WebSocket proxies and private ingress. Its four base/head cases recorded these terminal observations:

  | Observation | Base | This head |
  | --- | --- | --- |
  | Second client's path on the reused HTTP connection | `/forged` | `/owner` |
  | First client's body bytes at ingress | 1 | 31 |
  | Alternate local socket received an upgrade | yes | no |
  | Colon-query WebSocket path at configured ingress | `/ws?session=agent` | `/ws?session=agent:main:main` |

  The colon-query upgrade returned 101 on this head. Benign HTTP and WebSocket controls worked on both revisions. The run used local synthetic Iroh streams; it did not invoke a remote peer or model.
- Focused tests passed on this head: proxy boundary (7), protocol tunnel (7), workspace upload reader (16), and tunnel headers (2). The upload reader's framed-request regression failed before its adjustment and passed after it.
- Production and touched-test typechecks, targeted lint, formatting, and diff checks passed. A current-head independent diff review found no actionable issue.
- CI completed with one underlying failure: the test-line ratchet remained 18 lines above its CI ceiling after both tracked allocations exactly covered this PR's 225 net test lines. The aggregate gate failed because of that job; other selected checks passed. The local pinned-base check shows 21 inherited lines above its ceiling. No shared baseline or unrelated tests were changed.
